comments.note: MovieEditorViewModel.LoadAsync creates a new TaggerViewModel on each call. TaggerViewModel subscribes to ITagsManager.DataChanged in its constructor but never unsubscribes. If LoadAsync is called more than once (e.g. after an ApplyChanges that replaces _originalMovie), the prior TaggerVm retains a live DataChanged subscription, causing a memory leak. No test covers this scenario. A future WP should add a Dispose/cleanup call when TaggerVm is replaced.

comments.note: TaggerViewModel DataChanged subscription leak: LoadAsync creates a new TaggerViewModel that subscribes to _tagsManager.DataChanged, but MovieEditorViewModel never unsubscribes it. Since ITagsManager is a DI singleton with a longer lifetime than MovieEditorViewModel, the old TaggerVm is kept alive by the DataChanged delegate list until the app exits or the ITagsManager is disposed. Severity: medium. Path to fix: add IDisposable to TaggerViewModel (unsubscribes in Dispose) and dispose from MovieEditorViewModel. This requires a dedicated WP and is consistent with the acknowledged tech debt from WP-017.

MoviePropertiesViewModel is constructed inline inside ShowPropertiesCommand. Both MovieEditorViewModel and MoviePropertiesViewModel are in VideoIndexer.App.ViewModels (same layer), so this is architecturally acceptable — cross-layer calls must go through Core interfaces, but same-layer direct instantiation is fine. The IMoviePropertiesService interface correctly abstracts the dialog display, so the coupling is to a concrete construction shape within the same layer. No interface abstraction overhead warranted for a single-caller relationship.

CanMoveActorUp() only checks SelectedActorIndex > 0 but not SelectedActorIndex < ActorList.Count. An out-of-range selected index (positive but beyond list bounds) could cause an IndexOutOfRangeException in ActorList[idx] if the UI selection model were to allow it. In practice the UI ListBox resets selection when items change, and SelectedActorIndex is reset to -1 in RebuildActorList, so this edge case cannot occur. The redundant double-guard in MoveActorUp() (calls CanMoveActorUp() again before acting) provides an extra safety net. Acceptable.

LoadAsync has no re-entry guard. The doc comment says 'called once after construction, before the view becomes visible,' but nothing prevents a second call in unexpected usage. A second call would re-create TaggerVm (leaking the first subscription) and reset SelectedActorIndex/-1, disrupting any in-flight selection. Adding `if (TaggerVm is not null) return;` (or a dedicated `_isLoaded` bool) would make the single-call invariant explicit in code. This is Fix-Forward eligible but deferred because a proper fix needs IDisposable cleanup for the old TaggerVm first.

[documentation-forward] LoadAsync single-call invariant should be documented in api-surface.md: 'LoadAsync must be called exactly once after construction, before the view is shown. Calling it a second time creates a second TaggerViewModel with an unmanaged DataChanged subscription; a future IDisposable implementation will guard against this.' Also note that MovieEditorViewModel itself will need IDisposable when TaggerViewModel.Dispose is added.
